pll2d3c1-d1e3514.summary: Having shown where the angels were when created, proposes to examine what they were like at the beginning of their creation.

pll2d3c1-d1e3517.summary: Lists four things given to angels at creation: simple essence, indivisible and immaterial; personal distinctness; by naturally implanted reason, understanding, memory, and will or love; and free choice, the free faculty of inclining the will to good or evil, without violence or coercion.
claims: Angels have simple essence, personhood, intellect and will, and free choice.
Free choice can turn to good or evil without coercion.

pl-l2d3c1.summary: Turns from where the angels were to what they were like at creation. Four things were given them: a simple, indivisible, immaterial essence; personal distinctness; reason with understanding, memory, and will or love; and free choice, the faculty of turning the will to good or evil without force or coercion.
claims: Angels have a simple, indivisible, immaterial essence.
Angels have reason, with understanding, memory, and will.
Angels have free choice to turn to good or evil without coercion.
